findings.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — Light-theme value for `.reply-to-tab`-area `a` silently changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70%, making the bold link much lighter on light themes; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))

mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` light value changed from 70% to 30% (much darker) and the pair is inverted relative to desktop/modal.scss:94; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))
desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the username in the light theme; likely a copy-paste of the adjacent `.title` rule
mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50% instead of preserving 30% and using $secondary 70% for dark

mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `h3` light value changed from 20% to 50%, inconsistent with desktop/topic-post.scss:321 which preserves 20%/80%, making mobile link-summary headings noticeably lighter on light themes

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — Light-theme value for `.reply-to-tab`-area `a` silently changed from scale-color($primary, 30%) to 70%, making the bold link much lighter on light themes; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss the `a` inside the reply-to-tab area changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. This indeed alters the light-theme (first argument) from 30% to 70%, making it much lighter than before, and it also breaks the consistent pattern elsewhere in the diff (primary 30% pairs with secondary 70%). The proposed corrected form matches that pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` light value changed from 70% to 30% (much darker) and the pair is inverted relative to desktop/modal.scss:94; should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 70%), scale-color($secondary, 30%))

adjudication.rationale: The diff shown does not include `mobile/modal.scss` at all, so the cited location `mobile/modal.scss:102` and the alleged change there are not verifiable from this patch. The only visible `.custom-message-length` change is in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`, where it changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, which matches what the finding suggests as the desired form—not an inversion or a 70%→30% darkening in the primary value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the username in the light theme; likely a copy-paste of the adjacent `.title` rule

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any change to a `.name` rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss`, nor any change from a 30% to 50% lightness there. The only `.name` change visible in the provided diff is in `common/base/user.scss`, where `.name` remains at 30% lightness but is wrapped in `dark-light-choose(...)`. Since the alleged `desktop/user.scss:522` change is not present/visible in the diff, the finding is not verifiable from this patch.
